title: Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines): Cancellation on the Sale of the Insured Home
content:
## Scope

A cancellation of an Excess Flood policy because the insured home was sold, where the Tidemark HomeFlood policy whose policy number is the underlying policy number on the policy record has been cancelled for that sale, is signed by the named insured, and its returned premium is figured under the sale cancellation rule, in place of the pro rata method with minimum earned premium.

For such a sale cancellation the named insured signs the cancellation request when the cancellation is made and that signature is the signed request on file, and the cancellation is made only on a policy whose status is pending effective or active, which it leaves cancelled.

## When the returned premium is fixed

The returned premium on a sale cancellation is not fixed until every claim on the policy whose latest adjuster report documents more loss of use than has been paid carries a loss-of-use payment issued after that report.

In other words, while any claim on the policy has a latest adjuster report that documents more loss of use than the loss-of-use payments issued on that claim, and no loss-of-use payment issued after that report stands on the claim, the returned premium on a sale cancellation is not yet fixed.

## Capability

`sign_excess_sale_cancellation_a26754a5` records the named insured's signature cancelling their Excess Flood policy because the insured home was sold, with the settlement statement as the supporting document. One call records the signed cancellation request (reason: property sold), sets the policy to cancelled with the cancellation effective date given and today as the processing date, credits the returned premium given as a cancellation credit of the term premium of the current term together with the surplus lines tax and stamping fee on it at the rates recorded on the policy (an item that comes to 0.00 is not credited), and refunds the total credited to the insured with a refund reference. The amount owed on the policy falls by the credits and rises by the refund. Success is observable as the cancelled status, the signed request, the credit items and the refund on the account.

## How it is invoked

This is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks `sign_excess_sale_cancellation_a26754a5` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to sign the cancellation.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `excess_policy_id` | the reference number of the insured's Excess Flood policy, as returned by the Excess Flood policy lookup | identifier, as returned |
| `cancellation_effective_date` | the date the cancellation takes effect | calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD |
| `returned_premium` | the term premium returned on the cancellation before taxes | US dollars, 2 decimal places, already rounded to the cent |

## Return

On success, a confirmation sentence stating the signed request's reference number, the policy status (cancelled), the effective date (YYYY-MM-DD), the returned premium, the surplus lines tax and stamping fee returned (USD, 2 decimal places), the total refunded to the insured (USD, 2 decimal places) and the refund reference (text). If no Excess Flood policy has the reference number given, the string says so and nothing is recorded.
